title: Cohort plan hierarchy and fan-out execution
summary: A ratified cohort plan MUST hold one parent specification and one child specification per unit of work, and MUST execute as ordered groups of parallel delivery runs, where each run owns its own worktree, each group merges before the next one starts, and every ordering decision rests on durable records rather than agent judgment.
instructions: The ratified artifact MUST hold one parent specification carrying the complete record of the request, and one child specification for each unit of work a single delivery run owns.
A child specification MUST reach its parent through an audited reference stating the parent path, the selected range, the content digest, and the read trigger, and MUST NOT reproduce the parent body.
For its own unit of work a child specification governs, and for context that spans units the parent governs; each child MUST state that relationship.

Every requirement, constraint, out-of-scope statement, and open question of the request MUST appear across the child specifications exactly once, as owned, shared, or deferred, and the parent MUST keep the complete record.
A unit of work MUST own one coherent operator outcome, carry independently testable acceptance criteria, and reach a valid standalone completion state.

Splitting the ratified scope MUST reduce implementation and review risk by more than the coordination cost of the extra delivery runs it creates; when it does not, the plan MUST stay whole and MUST state why.
Units of work MUST be grouped into ordered groups numbered from 1, where no unit depends on another unit of its own group and every dependency names a unit of an earlier group.
When the ratified scope stays one unit, the artifact MUST record the reason the work remains serial.
Each unit of work MUST execute in its own Git worktree on its own branch, so two concurrent runs never mutate one workspace.
The harness MUST hold the execution graph, the group assignment, each unit's run id, and each group's completion proof in one durable record under runtime/logs/cohorts/.
A group MUST be treated as complete only when every one of its runs reports success in that run's own state and the durable record holds the merge proof for that group.
Starting a group MUST be refused while an earlier group is incomplete, and the refusal MUST name the session, the refused group, and the earlier group that blocks it.
Advancing one bound run directly MUST meet the same refusal, so the ordering blocker cannot be bypassed by working around the group command.
Merging a completed group into its base branch MUST be an explicit operator command, and it MUST write the merge proof only after the merge lands cleanly.
A run that has not succeeded, a workspace with uncommitted work, or a conflicting merge MUST leave the merge proof unwritten and the next group blocked.
Excluding one unit from a group MUST be an operator decision recorded with the operator's stated reason.
Removing a unit's workspace MUST be refused while its run is live or its workspace holds uncommitted work, unless the operator explicitly forces the removal.
Creating the runs of a group MUST perform no source-control action beyond adding worktrees; committing, merging, pushing, and branch deletion stay operator-owned.

Every run of a group MUST reach the shared context of the ratified plan through an audited reference that states the source path, the content digest, and the read trigger, and it MUST NOT receive a copy of that context.

Starting the first group automatically MUST require an explicit operator opt-in recorded when the run was created, MUST fire only for an approval of that ratified plan by the operator or by an away-mode decision applied on the operator's behalf, and MUST leave the recorded approval and the ratified plan unchanged when it fails.
An automatic start that fails MUST report the concrete error together with the manual commands that perform the same work.
Each unit MUST run the `delivery-chunk` workflow and MUST end at a verified implementation on its own branch. Release preparation MUST happen once, on the integrated result, never per unit.

The number of concurrent unit runs MUST NOT exceed the parallelism limit recorded on the session (`pan cohort init --max-parallel`, default 4). `pan cohort start` MUST create runs only for the free slots, MUST name the deferred units, and MUST be run again to start them once a unit run reaches a terminal state.

One operator session MAY supervise every live unit run of the active group at once. It MUST launch the ready worker of each distinct run in the same message so the launches execute in parallel, MUST keep every launch foreground, MUST observe each launched run with its own `pan watch <run-id>`, and MUST perform each run's pending action independently so one gated or stalled run never blocks its siblings.
A cohort supervisor MUST NOT launch two workers for one run, and MUST NOT launch a nested supervisor for a unit run.

Committing a finished unit branch stays operator-owned. A supervisor commits a unit worktree only under an explicit operator directive that covers that commit, MUST commit only that worktree's changes, and MUST name the unit id and run id in the commit message.
